summary: Both halves inspected, with enlargements of respect, the two C superscripts and the first The. The word partial is an above-line typed addition, unlike handwritten Kan- and with. The sp of respect carries a pen correction independent of the Kan- insertion curve. The old C superscripts remain unreadable under live handwritten n,p. The last cancelled fragment after opera is clipped at the right edge and remains doubtful. The lower-half degree has no secure accent. The author explicitly leaves direct sum versus direct product and positive-degree truncation unresolved in the wrong-quadrant totalization; the dual construction has a separate quasicoherence problem.

edits.reason: The enlarged sp has dark freehand retracing and a long p descender. It is separate from the Kan- placement curve; preserve the uncertain older sp-like impressions.
The overtyped final fragment is cut by the right edge. The proposed tor is plausible but its extent is not wholly visible, so mark the doubt.
The enlarged live h has typewriter serifs, with a displaced older h-like impression below; retain uncertainty in the older layer and identify the live typing.
The lower-half word has ordinary unaccented degree; no distinct acute stroke can be identified above its e.
